findings.static_call_chain: external Ruby input -> parser/compiler -> VM closure/env handling -> mrb_env_unshare
findings.attacker_controlled_data: Ruby source input controls closure creation, environment lifetime, object references, and GC pressure
findings.reachability_evidence: The fuzzer executes Ruby source through the ordinary mruby VM, which can create closures and exercise env unshare during block/env lifetime transitions.
findings.required_conditions: Input must construct closure/env state and GC pressure so mrb_env_unshare copies or updates env stack while object lifetime/write-barrier state is unsafe.
findings.root_cause: The candidate is a write-barrier/lifetime bug around mrb_env_unshare and environment stack copying. Dynamic validation must prove the exact operation is reached before treating any crash as matching this candidate.
findings.verification_plan: Submit small runnable Ruby programs early, inspect exact SymCC feedback for mrb_env_unshare, then refine closure and GC-state construction. A target operation hit is not a PoC; ASan reproduction is still required.

target_condition.why: p != NULL branch that controls whether stack_copy executes

observability_targets.why: Exact operation marker for the env stack copy; function or block entry alone is not enough.
